transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Murphy (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (FinSight CTO), Liu Chen (ML Engineer), Aisha Khan (Infra), Meera Patel (PM)

Summary: Quick sync on onboarding progress, access setup (VPC/IAM/KMS), and environment readiness for the pilot. Reviewed initial benchmark drops, discussed tuning (quantization, batching, KV cache) and next steps to complete the pilot.

Topics: onboarding status, network access, security docs, initial perf results, tuning recommendations, next steps / responsibilities

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. agenda today is pretty short - onboarding checks, access status, and the perf readouts priya will run through the initial numbers.
[00:18] Carlos (FinSight): yep thanks alex, we have about 40 minutes. quick note, Meera might drop in the last 10 to confirm timelines.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): cool, i'll start with the access matrix - last week we requested VPC peering details and a test IAM role for the service account. any updates on that?
[00:36] Aisha (FinSight Infra): we got the peering request, just waiting on the CIDR confirmation from security. i'll have that by tomorrow EOD. iam role still pending, we were clarifying the minimum permissions.
[00:45] Alex (Redwood): that works - if you share the exact principal we can provision the test endpoint credentials. don't forget KMS access for key unwrap, we need kms:Decrypt and iam:PassRole for the service role.
[00:56] Aisha (FinSight): noted, we'll add those perms. question - for private deployment do we need any extra open ports?
[01:03] Priya (Redwood SE): for the private (vpc) flow, only internal cluster comms on 9090 and 50051 for grpc. no internet egress required for model serving, only for control plane telemetry unless you opt out.
[01:16] Liu (FinSight ML): good. about the model variants - we've been testing with the 13B open model you suggested. initial token latency looks okay but throughput is lower than expected under burst.
[01:27] Priya (Redwood SE): okay, two things - kv cache and batching config. by default we had batching at 64ms window which favors latency; if you switch to 150ms window for batched requests you should see throughput jump but p99 latency increases. also kv cache hit rate is low because your request prefixes vary a lot in the test set.
[01:45] Carlos (FinSight): can you quantify? we need p95 < 300ms for interactive analytics, and cost needs to stay under our pilot budget.
[01:54] Priya (Redwood SE): from the short run - p50 was ~120ms on hosted, p95 ~320ms with current batching. if we enable 8-bit quant plus a slightly bigger micro-batching (batch target 6 requests / 150ms) we saw p95 drop to around 260ms in our internal sims, and token cost down ~18%.
[02:16] Liu (FinSight): interesting, are there tradeoffs on hallucination/quality with 8-bit?
[02:21] Priya (Redwood SE): small increase in variance, we recommend running your eval set - we can roll canary with q4 -> compare rouge/accuracy on sample prompts before full switch.
[02:33] Meera (FinSight PM): quick question on logs and observability - where will the request traces land, and how long do you retain token-level logs for the pilot?
[02:41] Jon (Redwood CSM): for hosted we keep token-level traces for 30 days by default, can extend with an add-on; for Dedicated/Private you control retention in the cluster, and we provide hooks to forward to your ELK or DataDog. we'll include the retention matrix in the docs we send.
[02:55] Carlos (FinSight): we also need SOC2 docs and the network diagram for our security team.
[03:00] Alex (Redwood): yes we'll send SOC2 summary and a network topology diagram. also will include KMS integration docs and recommended IAM policies.
[03:06] Aisha (FinSight): perfect. about the VPC peering - any known gotchas? we've done peering before but want to avoid asymmetric routing issues.
[03:15] Priya (Redwood SE): main thing is to ensure the peering routes both ways and that your security groups allow the ports i mentioned. also if you have strict egress rules, our control plane callbacks for metrics need explicit allow, or we can flip to offline metrics upload.
[03:29] Liu (FinSight): for the benchmark, can we run an on-prem test instead of hosted? we want to check throughput on our target GPU shape.
[03:36] Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely - for Private pilot we'll provide a containerized runtime and config script. you'll need to provide GPU nodes with nvlink and at least 80GB vram for the 13B quantized baseline, or we can advise on sharding. we'll also provide a perf harness (wrk-style) for consistent results.
[03:52] Carlos (FinSight): timeline wise, we want a production-ish run by the end of the pilot (3 weeks). is that feasible if we get access this week?
[03:59] Alex (Redwood): yes, if access is granted this week and we do the two benchmark runs and a small canary rollout, that fits. main dependencies are IAM/VPC + KMS.
[04:10] Meera (FinSight): ok, sounds good. regarding pricing - any estimate on cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our expected qps?
[04:18] Jon (Redwood CSM): rough ballpark - hosted unit costs are slightly higher but zero infra ops; Dedicated reserved pool gives ~30-40% lower per-token cost at commit levels. we'll send a tailored cost compare once you share expected qps and token mix.
[04:33] Carlos (FinSight): competitor question - are you supporting alternative floating point or custom kernels we might have seen on Anthropic roadmap?
[04:40] Priya (Redwood SE): we select kernels per model/hardware and support integer quant paths (8-bit) and optimized attention kernels on the common GPU shapes. if you have a specific kernel, we can test.
[04:50] Liu (FinSight): ok next steps for the bench: we will share sample traces and target SLOs by Friday, aisha will add the test role and confirm peering, redwood to share security pack and run the initial hosted benchmark and then a private run once infra is ready.
[05:05] Alex (Redwood): correct - i'll follow up with the security packet and the runbook. priya will schedule the benchmark slot and provide the quant/batching config we recommend.
[05:14] Priya (Redwood SE): i'll also include a small guide on how to set cache-friendly prefixes for higher KV hit rate, saves a lot on token cost if your workloads have repeated seeds.
[05:25] Aisha (FinSight): one more operational question - for canary deploys how do rollbacks work if quality regresses?
[05:31] Priya (Redwood SE): we support canary -> automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval set; you can define thresholds on latency and on eval metrics. we also keep the previous model variant alive for fast fallback.
[05:46] Carlos (FinSight): cool. any blockers from redwood side?
[05:50] Alex (Redwood): none - we're waiting on your access pieces.
[05:54] Meera (FinSight): ok, wrap up then. thanks everyone.
[05:58] Alex (Redwood): thanks all, we'll send the security doc and a short checklist. meeting notes / action items will be in the follow-up.

End of transcript.
